content: A mucocele, also known as a mucus extravasation phenomenon, is a swelling of the connective tissue caused by the accumulation of mucin that leaks from a ruptured salivary gland duct. This condition is most often triggered by localized trauma. Mucoceles typically appear as bluish, translucent swellings and are more frequently observed in children and young adults. The most common site for a mucocele is the surface of the lower lip. However, they can also occur on the inner lining of the cheek, referred to as the buccal mucosa, as well as on the anterior ventral surface of the tongue and the floor of the mouth. When a mucocele develops on the floor of the mouth, it is specifically termed a ranula. Mucoceles are rarely found on the upper lip. The size of mucoceles can range from as small as 1 millimeter to several centimeters in diameter. Upon palpation, they may feel fluctuant, though some can present as firm. Their duration can vary significantly, lasting anywhere from a few days to several years. Mucoceles may exhibit recurrent swelling and can occasionally rupture, releasing their contents. A specific variant of mucoceles, known as superficial mucoceles, can occur on the palate, retromolar pad, and posterior buccal mucosa. These present as single or multiple vesicles that eventually rupture, forming ulcers. Although these superficial mucoceles typically heal within a few days, they tend to recur in the same location. Histologically, mucoceles are characterized by granulation tissue surrounding pools of mucin. Due to the concurrent inflammatory response, neutrophils and foamy histiocytes are commonly observed in the affected tissue. Treatment for mucoceles varies depending on the severity and persistence of the condition. Some mucoceles resolve spontaneously without intervention. However, chronic mucoceles often require surgical removal. In cases where recurrence is a concern, the adjacent salivary gland may also be excised to prevent further episodes. Surgical options include traditional excision as well as advanced techniques such as laser surgery and minimally invasive procedures, which significantly reduce recovery time.
